meta.incident: Al-Ahli Arab Hospital / Al-Maamadani / Baptist Hospital courtyard explosion, Gaza City
meta.purpose: Primary and secondary sources across competing claims. Not a verdict. Read originals.
notes_for_reviewer: No public munition remnant photos exist. That is the single biggest forensic gap.

Gaza Health Ministry claimed 471 killed / 342 injured. Anglican Diocese (hospital operator) said ~200 killed. US intel said 100-300, likely low end. HRW said MoH ratio looks inconsistent with visible damage.
Consensus of US/UK/FR/CA intel + AP/CNN/HRW: not a large Israeli air-dropped bomb; more consistent with a rocket-type munition. Attribution of launcher is the contested part.
Forensic Architecture + Earshot + Channel 4 contest IDF trajectory/propellant/video claims and argue northeast origin (Israel-controlled direction).
FA later walked back an early 'artillery shell' claim and said projectile was probably a rocket, while keeping the northeast-origin argument.

competing_theses.A_palestinian_rocket_misfire: Unguided rocket (often attributed to PIJ) launched from Gaza toward Israel failed shortly after launch; warhead + leftover propellant exploded in crowded courtyard.
competing_theses.B_munition_from_israel_direction: Projectile arrived from northeast (Israel-controlled perimeter). Not necessarily a large JDAM. Could be rocket, missile, or artillery-class munition. FA/Earshot.
competing_theses.C_israeli_airstrike_as_initially_claimed: Israeli aircraft bomb on hospital. Physical crater and building damage do not match typical Israeli air-dropped HE bombs used in Gaza.

physical_observations_repeated_across_so.crater_approx: Roughly 0.6-1.0 m across, 0.3-0.4 m deep (HRW photogrammetry ~90 x 60 x 30-40 cm; CNN ~3x3 ft, 1 ft deep; French intel similar).
physical_observations_repeated_across_so.damage_pattern: Burned cars, broken windows, pockmarks, fireball. Hospital buildings largely standing. Limited structural collapse.
physical_observations_repeated_across_so.location: Paved courtyard / parking lot between landscaped areas, crowded with civilians sheltering.
physical_observations_repeated_across_so.missing_evidence: No published photos of munition fragments/casing/guidance kit. Gaza EOD seen at crater; remnants not released.

sources.stance: Balance of evidence: not Israeli airstrike; likely malfunctioning rocket from Gaza. Some video Israel cited was an unrelated Israeli-launched projectile.

sources.org: The New York Times Visual Investigations

Separate videos show Gaza rocket barrages minutes before blast
Does not by itself prove attribution

sources.stance: Cause still contested; crater much smaller than typical Israeli precision bomb; FA initially suggested artillery from Israel then revised to probably a rocket
key_claims: Experts: leftover fuel fire plausible

sources.stance: Apparent rocket-propelled munition of type commonly used by Palestinian armed groups; large air-dropped bomb highly unlikely; launcher not conclusively identified; independent investigation needed

Sound, fireball, crater, splatter, fragmentation consistent with rocket

Shallow channel into crater from NE

sources.stance: Disputes two core IDF claims: (1) Al Jazeera mid-air blast is the misfired PIJ rocket; (2) unspent propellant from the 17-rocket salvo caused the courtyard damage. Frames IDF material as disinformation.
key_claims: Mid-air explosion is an Israeli interceptor; fragments would take ~31s to fall from 5 km; hospital blast was ~8s later so that object cannot be the hit
All 17 rockets in the cited salvo stopped flaring after similar distance/speed (1.8-2 km, 500-630 m/s), consistent with burned-out motors, not leftover fuel at hospital
Israel has not produced conclusive visual evidence of a Hamas/PIJ rocket as the source
NYT and WaPo analyses cited as corroborating the interceptor-video point

sources.stance: Adds firsthand testimony of surgeon Dr Ghassan Abu-Sittah present at the hospital; used to challenge overlook of witness accounts
key_claims: FA says witness testimony was sidelined in early narrative fight

sources.stance: Doppler analysis: incoming sound not from SW Gaza as IDF claimed; possible firing points east of hospital. IDF 'Hamas intercept' audio assessed as two separately recorded channels edited together.

hard_unresolved_questions: Where are the munition fragments, and who last had custody?
If it was a Gaza rocket, which group and which launcher site?
If FA northeast origin is right, what specific Israeli or other munition class fits a tiny crater + large fireball?
How many people were actually in the courtyard, and how was 471 derived?
Is the IDF released audio authentic?
